title: Microsoft Teams: report a message or an external user for a security concern in US Government clouds
summary: The briefing leaves sharing reports with Microsoft as an unanswered question, but Microsoft's Teams security-report privacy page states that report data is shared for threat analysis and service protection. The roadmap facts, admin paths and PowerShell command are supported; the disagreement over Government cloud availability should also include the Teams reporting reference.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Government cloud users reporting suspicious Teams messages.
claims.quote: Users in Gov clouds can now report suspicious messages and external users within Teams.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Government cloud users reporting suspicious external users within Teams.
claims.quote: Users in Gov clouds can now report suspicious messages and external users within Teams.

claims.claim: The roadmap says reports surface in the Teams admin center for investigation and action.
claims.quote: Reports are surfaced in the Teams admin center, giving admins greater visibility into potentially malicious activity and enabling them to investigate and take appropriate action.

claims.claim: The reporting signal is intended to help identify phishing, impersonation, spam and other messaging threats.
claims.quote: By incorporating end-user reports as an additional security signal, this capability helps organizations identify and respond more quickly to phishing, impersonation, spam, and other messaging threats.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users report a chat or channel message through ... > Report this message > Security concern.
claims.quote: Go to chat or channel message and select ... > Report this message. ... Select Security concern.

claims.claim: The Defender instructions label the selection Security risk - Spam, phishing, malicious content.
claims.quote: If reporting for Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance is turned off, users might not have the dropdown list to select Security risk - Spam, phishing, malicious content. Instead, they're shown a confirmation pop-up.
claims.fix: After the sentence giving the Defender label, add: 'If reporting for Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance is turned off, users might see a confirmation pop-up instead of the selection.' Keep the existing submissions-teams citation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Reporting an external user happens while blocking that user.
claims.quote: User can report suspicious external users while blocking them in Teams, from external chat requests and user profile cards.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can select Report this person while blocking someone from an external chat request.
claims.quote: Open the external chat request. ... Select Block, Delete or Leave, depending on the chat type and your organization's settings, and follow the prompt to block the user. ... Click Report this person checkbox and confirm.

claims.claim: Users can select Report this person while blocking someone from the person's profile card.
claims.quote: Open the user's profile card. ... Open the menu option and select Block contact ... Click Report this person checkbox and confirm.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Teams admin center path is Messaging policies > policy > Report a security concern.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Messaging policies. ... Select a policy. ... Turn on the setting: Report a security concern.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting $true.
claims.quote: -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting: This setting determines if users can report any security concern posted in message to their admin. Possible values: True, False

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Scope: Users; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The messaging policy's Report a security concern setting determines whether its users can report messages and external users.
claims.quote: Users can submit reports only when the required reporting settings are enabled in the Teams admin center. ... For chat and channel messages and external users, the Report a security concern setting must be turned on in the user's messaging policy.

claims.claim: Viewing or configuring user reporting in the Teams admin center requires Global Administrator or Teams Administrator.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in the Teams admin center, you need to be a member of the Global Administrator or Teams Administrator roles.

claims.claim: Learn identifies Settings & policies as the entry point for the policy in the new experience.
claims.quote: To access this policy in the new experience, go to Settings & policies.

claims.claim: Cloud availability for this messaging policy setting is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Report a security concern GCC GCC High DoD default AllowSecurityEndUserReporting licensing. Read end-user-reporting-security, submissions-teams, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy and utcm-teams-resources; none specifies cloud availability of this setting.

claims.claim: The report is reached through Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > Report > User reported security submissions.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. ... On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions.
claims.fix: Add to the cloud-disagreement paragraph: 'The Teams reporting reference also lists User reported security submissions as unavailable in GCC, GCC High and DoD, in contrast to the roadmap.' Cite and add to sources https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-analytics-and-reports/teams-reporting-reference#teams-reporting-reference; its table lists Public Yes, GCC No, GCCH No and DoD No for this report.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The report categories are Calling, Chats and channels, and User.
claims.quote: Under Report category, choose one of the following categories: Calling; Chats and channels; User.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Admins can export the user-reported security submissions reports to CSV.
claims.quote: The User reported security submissions report in the Microsoft Teams admin center helps you review security-related reports submitted by users in your organization. You can export these reports to a CSV file for further analysis.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls; Open questions: API
claims.claim: An API or export feed for reading User reported security submissions is not documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams user reported security submissions report API Microsoft Graph export reports; "user reported security submissions" API PowerShell. Read the report page, utcm-teams-resources and Graph security-threatsubmission; none documents an API for this report.

claims.claim: The Chats and channels CSV includes the sender's domain.
claims.quote: Sender domain name: Domain of the sender. This field might be blank if the sender uses a consumer account, depending on their privacy setting. ... Available only in the exported CSV file.

claims.claim: The Chats and channels CSV participant list contains at most 20 entries.
claims.quote: Participant list: List of participants in the conversation, including their display name, email address, and Microsoft Resource Identifier (MRI). Maximum 20 entries: up to 10 entries from the reporter's tenant and up to 10 entries from non-reporter tenants.

claims.claim: The exported report includes any optional reporter comments.
claims.quote: Reporter comments: Optional comments that the reporter user sent along with the report, if any. ... Available only in the exported CSV file.

claims.claim: The User report includes the reported user's display name and email address if available.
claims.quote: Reported user name: Reported user's display name and email address, if available. If the reported user uses a consumer account, their email address might not be available depending on their privacy setting.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Admins can use the reported user's identifier to block that user on the Teams admin center External Access page.
claims.quote: Reported user ID: Microsoft Resource Identifier (MRI) of the reported user. Admins can use this identifier when blocking the user on the External Access page of the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The Defender page says message content is copied when a Teams item is reported to Microsoft.
claims.quote: When a user reports a Teams item to Microsoft, the following data associated with the item is copied and included in ongoing algorithm reviews, as applicable: Message content.

claims.claim: The Defender page says up to fifteen messages before and after the reported message might be shared for analysis.
claims.quote: The submission might also include contextual data for the reported message. Specifically, up to fifteen messages before and after the reported message might also be shared for analysis.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether the specific fifteen-message contextual-sharing behavior applies to Government cloud reports.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reporting Government analysis Microsoft security concern; "security-report-privacy" "Government". Read submissions-teams and security-report-privacy; neither specifies fifteen-message contextual sharing for Government clouds.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Message senders are not notified that their messages were reported.
claims.quote: Message senders aren't notified their messages were reported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can report the same item multiple times.
claims.quote: Users can report the same items multiple times.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Reporting is initiated by the user.
claims.quote: Users who see a concerning chat or a channel message in Teams can report it as a security risk. ... Review the selections and select Report.

claims.claim: The report supplies information for a separate administrator blocking action rather than describing automatic administrator blocking.
claims.quote: Reported user ID: Microsoft Resource Identifier (MRI) of the reported user. Admins can use this identifier when blocking the user on the External Access page of the Teams admin center.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn says external-user reporting is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender, unlike message reporting.
claims.quote: Only user reporting of messages is supported in Microsoft Defender as of now. User reporting of external users is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender.

claims.claim: Message reports require the Teams reporting setting and the Defender reporting setting to be on to appear correctly on Submissions > User reported.
claims.quote: If "Report a security concern" is turned on in the Teams admin center, it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported messages to show up correctly on the User reported tab on the Submissions page.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: End user reporting for Security describes reporting in organizations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report malicious messages in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Defender user-reporting page lists Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report messages, calls, meetings, or meeting participants in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: The admin center report's prerequisites name reporting settings but no license.
claims.quote: Reported interactions appear in the User reported security submissions reports only after users submit reports. ... Users can submit reports only when the required reporting settings are enabled in the Teams admin center.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects the documented included-subscription and add-on acquisition routes.
claims.quote: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2 (add-on licenses or included in subscriptions like Microsoft 365 E5)

claims.where: Open questions: reports sent to Microsoft or retained only in the tenant
claims.claim: Whether reports from US Government tenants are also sent to Microsoft for analysis, rather than staying only in the tenant's Teams admin center report, remains undocumented.
claims.quote: You might report security concerns that involve Teams communications, including messages, calls, meetings, or users. ... Report data is also shared with Microsoft for threat analysis and service protection.
claims.fix: Replace the open question 'Are reports from US Government tenants also sent to Microsoft for analysis, or do they stay in the tenant's Teams admin center report?' with 'Microsoft states that Teams security-report data is also shared with Microsoft for threat analysis and service protection.' Cite and add to sources https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/security-report-privacy. This general data-handling rule does not establish the Government-specific fifteen-message contextual-sharing detail.

claims.where: front matter: action; Why it matters
claims.claim: The prepare action rating agrees with the page's account of an unknown-default optional capability with no stated change to existing behavior.
claims.quote: action: "prepare" ... Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival in these clouds, so no source says existing behaviour changes.
claims.fix: Set action to 'review'. The assessment scale assigns review to a new capability with an unstated default when no source says existing behavior changes; the page's own arrival-behavior paragraph takes that position.

claims.quote: Users can report messages in Teams chats or channels that are incorrectly flagged by Link Protection as containing malicious URLs. ... In the report dialog that opens, select Not a security concern.
